title: T1667 — Email Bombing
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Email Bombing with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: Target picked
steps.caption: The attacker collects an employee's address, for example from a website or a leaked list.
steps.defender: nothing is visible yet. No logs show anything, because no mail has been sent.

steps.title: Bot signups
steps.caption: Automated bots type the victim's address into hundreds of newsletter forms that skip email confirmation.
steps.defender: if someone looks, a trickle of "welcome" emails from unknown domains starts arriving. Nothing alerts yet.

steps.title: Inbox flood
steps.caption: Welcome and confirmation emails arrive in waves, thousands within a few hours. A counter on the mailbox climbs fast.
steps.defender: message trace shows an abnormal inbound rate for one recipient, spread over dozens of unrelated sender domains.

steps.title: Real alert buried
steps.caption: A genuine security email - an MFA test push confirmation or password-reset notice - lands in the inbox and is pushed out of sight within seconds.
steps.defender: the platform still delivered the real alert normally. Only message-trace and audit logs prove it existed.

steps.title: Fake IT call
steps.caption: The attacker phones or Teams-calls the victim, claiming to be IT support fixing the "email problem".
steps.defender: no mail evidence. A call log or a help-desk system entry may be the only trace, if one is recorded at all.

steps.title: Access granted
steps.caption: The victim follows the caller's instructions and allows a remote-assist session or re-registers MFA.
steps.defender: the identity platform writes an audit event, for example "User registered security info". This is the first loud, high-value signal.

steps.title: MFA stolen
steps.caption: The attacker adds their own authenticator device and reads the mailbox, hunting for invoices and vendor threads.
steps.defender: new sign-in and mailbox-access events from unusual locations, plus new MFA methods the user never owned.

steps.title: SOC response
steps.caption: The SOC correlates the mail-volume spike, the help-desk contact, and the MFA change. Sessions are revoked, the user is verified by a callback to a known number, and the bot sources are blocked.
steps.defender: correlated alerts in the SIEM plus containment actions in the audit trail.
